metadata.title: Nebula
metadata.description: Super Mario Galaxy, running natively on Windows, Linux, macOS and Android, in every language, with high refresh rates, mods and achievements.

available.paragraph_1: The first beta of Nebula v2, for Windows, Linux, macOS and Android.

v2.paragraph_1: Nebula runs Super Mario Galaxy as native code, built from SMGCommunity’s Petari decompilation. You need your own copy of the game.
v2.paragraph_3: All US, PAL and JP languages are supported, each through its own language’s ISO.
v2.paragraph_4: Interpolation for displays faster than 60 Hz.
v2.paragraph_5: Internal resolution up to 4K, aspect ratios from 4:3 to 32:9, and DLSS, FSR 3, XeSS and MetalFX upscaling.
v2.paragraph_6: Keyboard and mouse, Xbox, PlayStation, Switch, Steam and generic controllers, and the Wii Remote.
v2.paragraph_7: Cutscene skip, instant dialogue and an in-game settings menu.
v2.paragraph_8: .luma mods, Riivolution packs, Dolphin texture packs and replacement movies.
v2.paragraph_9: Achievement pop-ups and a progress board in the Comet Observatory.
v2.paragraph_10: Import saves from a Wii, Dolphin or the Switch release, and back them up to a ZIP file.

start.paragraph_1: Windows 10 (1803 or newer) or 11 (64-bit), an x86-64 CPU with SSE4.2, a Direct3D 12 or 11 GPU, 8 GB RAM and 8 GB of free space for setup.
start.paragraph_2: You need Super Mario Galaxy for Wii (North America RMGE01, Europe RMGP01 or Japan RMGJ01). Import your ISO, RVZ or extracted game folder.
start.paragraph_3: Choose your game, install, then open Nebula from the Start menu. The setup guide covers the steps and your first settings.

support.paragraph_1: Donations go straight to keepvaibin through Ko-fi. Any amount is super welcome!
support.paragraph_2: Donating is completely optional and does not unlock anything. But any donations help build the features that you request!

community.paragraph_1: Announcements and setup help on Discord, and bug reports on GitHub.

questions.paragraph_1: Yes. Nebula is free software under the GNU GPL v3. You need your own copy of Super Mario Galaxy.
questions.paragraph_2: Yes, as a beta. Nebula v2.0.0-beta.1 is available now from the Download page. Expect faults, and keep a copy of your saves.
questions.paragraph_3: No. Nebula v2 is native code built from SMGCommunity’s Petari decompilation. Nebula v1.0.2 translates the game’s PowerPC code to C++ during setup.
questions.question_4: Which copy of the game do I need?
questions.paragraph_4: Super Mario Galaxy for Wii from North America (RMGE01), Europe (RMGP01) or Japan (RMGJ01), as an ISO, RVZ or extracted folder. Nebula v1.0.2 reads only the North American release, revision 0.
questions.question_5: Which platforms does Nebula run on?
questions.paragraph_5: Nebula v2 runs on Windows, Linux (including Steam Deck), macOS and Android. An iPhone and iPad version is in development. Nebula v1.0.2 runs on Windows.
questions.question_6: Can I use a Dolphin save?
questions.paragraph_6: Yes. Open Settings, then the GENERAL page, and choose Import saves. Nebula reads Dolphin, Wii and Switch saves. The save guide has the steps.
questions.paragraph_7: Most Riivolution packs, file replacements and Dolphin texture packs work. Wii code patches do not run in a native game. LumaLink converts memory patches and lists the rest.
questions.paragraph_8: No. Nebula is an independent project, not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Nintendo.
